title: Newick as a named tree string format
dek: Parentheses, commas, branch lengths, semicolons. Wikipedia format card. Not a substitution model.
story: Newick on Wikipedia is a file format: nested parentheses for topology, optional :lengths, a trailing semicolon. It is how software passes a tree, not how evolution happens.
A Newick string can encode a wrong tree as easily as a right one. Likelihood, bootstrap, and clock claims live elsewhere.
This card exists because pipelines fail on a missing semicolon more often than on Wilks.
deep: Quoted labels versus illegal characters are parser fights.
Internal node labels and posterior probabilities get stuffed into names — a convention, not a standard posterior.
Nexus is a neighbouring container format.
Do not paste a Newick into a paper as 'the model'.

visual.caption: String syntax stacked above the scientific objects it does not specify.
visual.annotation: A pretty string is not Q, not a clock, not a bootstrap.
